How do you know it still works tomorrow on traffic you've never seen? There are two kinds of evaluation and you need both. Offline and online evaluation are not the same job. Offline runs before you ship on a fixed set where you know the right answer, so you can compute correctness directly. Online runs in production on real questions with no labels where you cannot compute correctness at all. Same word, two completely different problems. Start with offline because it's the one you control. You build a golden set a circumflex euros, real questions with known good answers a circumflex euros, and you score your system against it. If MRR or faithfulness drops, the deploy is blocked a circumflex euros, the same way a failing unit test stops a release. A silent quality regression after a prompt tweak is exactly the bug this catches before a single user sees it. Then you ship and the ground truth disappears. In production, a user asks a question you've never seen and nobody labels whether the answer was right. You can't compute correctness live. So online monitoring changes the question a circumflex euros from is this answer correct to is the system behaving like it did when it was healthy. And the thing that makes both debuggable is the trace. For every request, a tool like LangSmith records the whole story. Which chunks were retrieved and at what scores, the exact prompt that was sent, what came back, and the latency of each stage a circumflex euros plus the tokens and cost. When a proxy alerts, the trace is where you find out why. In practice, the offline gate is small. Run the golden set, compute MRR, and fail the build if it slipped below the baseline.
